newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Telecom surges on stake sale talk.
newsitem.headline: HK Telecom surges on stake sale talk.

text.p: Shares of Hong Kong Telecommunications rose sharply on Friday on renewed speculation that parent Cable and Wireless Plc may sell a stake in the company, brokers said.
Hongkong Telecom rose 5.50 percent to a high of HK$13.50 before retreating slightly to HK$13.30 at mid-morning, up 50 cents on the day.
Analysts said market talk that C&W would possibly sell part of its 59 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom to Singapore Telecommunications Ltd boosted sentiment.
"If it is true about the rumour that Singapore Telecom would take a stake (in the company) that would be very good news," said Gary Chan, an analyst at UBS Securities said.
Hongkong Telecom's American Depository Receipts closed 7.5 percent higher in overseas last night.
A Hongkong Telecom spokeswoman said the company did not comment on market rumours.

Singapore Telecom has often been cited as a possible buyer of a stake in Hongkong Telecom. The company earlier this month commented that such a story was without foundation. Analysts also said the current weakness of property counters fuelled switching to utilities shares from properties.
UBS's Chan said the yield on Hongkong Telecom was strong and its current price/earnings multipule of about 11.7 time on earnings ending March 98 was considered low and attractive.
But some brokers remained cautious, saying worries over Hongkong Telecom's earning prospects might cap the share price.
